bazi.name: BaZi
bazi.background: BaZi, or "eight characters", is the classical Chinese Four Pillars method: your birth year, month, day and hour are each written as a Heavenly Stem and an Earthly Branch.
bazi.tagline: Your birth moment becomes four pillars of stems and branches, which we read through the Five Elements, the Ten Gods and ten-year Luck Pillars.
bazi.prepare: Your birth date and time. If you don't know the time you can still generate a chart, just without an hour pillar. Birthplace is optional and enables true solar time; gender sets the direction of the Luck Pillars.

seo.title: BaZi Four Pillars Chart: Day Master, Ten Gods and Luck Pillars
seo.description: Generate a BaZi chart by solar terms and explore your Five Elements balance, Ten Gods and Luck Pillars. Rule-based, with visible evidence, for cultural study and self-reflection.

tells.title: Day Master and temperament
tells.body: Your day stem, the Day Master, anchors the chart. Its symbolism and a strength score describe how you tend to go about things.

tells.title: Five Elements balance
tells.body: A weighted count of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water across stems, hidden stems and the month, with the elements this chart favors and those it finds less helpful.

tells.title: Ten Gods and chart structure
tells.body: Every other stem is read as one of the Ten Gods relative to the Day Master, such as Direct Officer or Eating God, and the month determines the chart's structure.

tells.title: Luck Pillars and annual pillars
tells.body: Ten Luck Pillars of ten years each, plus the annual pillars around today, give you a frame for reviewing and planning rather than a verdict.

method.title: Build the pillars from solar terms
method.body: The year changes at the exact moment of Lichun (Start of Spring) and months follow the twelve solar-term boundaries, not the lunar new year. With a birthplace, true solar time is on by default and can be switched off under advanced options.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: Element weights, strength scoring, Ten Gods, structures and auxiliary stars come from fixed rules, then map to entries in a structured knowledge base. The report's text is written in advance, not generated on the fly.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags naming the chart factors they used, so you can check them against your chart.

sample.caption: Four Pillars from a made-up birth moment

notes.text: You may feel comfortable providing a structure that others can use.
Wood 31%, Fire 13%, Earth 23%, Metal 18%, Water 16%. Favorable elements: Fire and Earth.
notes.basis: Weighted count of stems and hidden stems

notes.text: Luck Pillars run in reverse from about age 4 years 9 months. The first is Yi Chou, whose stem is the Direct Officer for this Day Master.
notes.basis: Year stem polarity, gender and the previous solar term

faq.q: What if I don't know my birth time?
faq.a: Tick "I don't know my birth time". We won't invent an hour pillar: the report uses the other three pillars, estimates the start of your Luck Pillars from local noon, and flags lower confidence.

faq.q: Why doesn't the BaZi year start at Lunar New Year?
faq.a: The year pillar changes at the exact moment of Lichun, usually around February 4, and months follow twelve solar-term boundaries. If you were born near Lichun, your year pillar may differ from the zodiac animal you usually hear.

faq.q: Do I need to calculate true solar time myself?
faq.a: No. When you enter a birthplace, we correct clock time for longitude and the equation of time, and use the corrected time by default. Without a birthplace, no correction is applied.

faq.q: How does gender affect the chart?
faq.a: It sets, together with the year stem's polarity, whether Luck Pillars run forward or in reverse. If you choose "Prefer not to say", we use the male rule and note this in the report.

faq.q: How is BaZi different from Zi Wei Dou Shu?
faq.a: BaZi works with stems, branches and the Five Elements, and can run without a birth time. Zi Wei Dou Shu places stars in twelve palaces and needs an exact birth time. They are separate systems that can be read side by side.

faq.q: Can the report tell me what will happen to me?
faq.a: No. It describes the chart's structure and how the tradition reads it, for cultural study and self-reflection. It makes no claims about specific events and does not replace medical, legal or financial advice.

more.label: How to read your Four Pillars

ziwei.name: Zi Wei Dou Shu
ziwei.background: Zi Wei Dou Shu, sometimes called Purple Star astrology, is a Chinese tradition that places a set of named stars into twelve palaces, each representing an area of life.
ziwei.tagline: Your lunar birth date and hour set the Life and Body Palaces, then fourteen major stars and many secondary stars are placed across twelve palaces.
ziwei.prepare: Your birth date and exact birth time (required). Birthplace is optional and enables true solar time; gender sets the direction of the Decade Periods.

seo.title: Zi Wei Dou Shu Chart: Twelve Palaces, Stars and Transformations
seo.description: Generate a Zi Wei Dou Shu chart from your lunar birth date and hour. Explore twelve palaces, the Four Transformations and Decade Periods, with visible evidence, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: Life Palace and temperament
tells.body: The major stars in your Life Palace, their brightness, and the supporting and challenging stars around them describe how you approach yourself and daily life.

tells.title: Twelve areas of life
tells.body: Career, Wealth, Spouse, Wellbeing and the other palaces each hold their own stars. Start from your question, then read the related palaces together.

tells.title: Transformations and configurations
tells.body: Hua Lu, Quan, Ke and Ji mark where themes shift, and the engine checks for traditional configurations such as Sha Po Lang.

tells.title: Decades and this year
tells.body: Ten-year Decade Periods and the current year are layered on your chart, each with its own transformations, so long and short cycles stay distinct.

method.title: Convert to lunar date and hour
method.body: Your birth moment is converted to a lunar date and one of twelve traditional hours. By default a leap month is split at the 15th day, and true solar time applies when you give a birthplace.

method.title: Place stars and match rules
method.body: Palaces, the Five Elements class and stars are placed by the open-source iztro library and checked by our engine. Transformations use the Zhongzhou table, configurations come from fixed rules, and results map to a structured knowledge base.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags naming the palaces, stars and brightness they used, so you can check them against the chart.

sample.caption: Summary of a chart from a made-up birth moment

notes.text: You may find a useful starting point in independent decisions and focused responses to a challenge.
notes.basis: Qi Sha in the Life Palace

notes.text: You can use this configuration to reflect on a practical tendency.
notes.basis: Lu Ma Jiao Chi and Sha Po Lang

faq.q: Can I do this without a birth time?
faq.a: No. The Life Palace and most stars depend on the hour, so the chart can't be built without it. The form offers a short questionnaire that ranks the twelve possible birth hours; treat its result as a starting point.

faq.q: How are leap months handled?
faq.a: By default the first half of a leap month counts as the previous month and the second half as the next. Advanced options let you assign the whole month to either one.

faq.q: Which school do you follow?
faq.a: Chart placement uses the open-source iztro library and the Zhongzhou transformation table, currently the only table offered. Other schools can give different results; the settings used are noted in the report.

faq.q: Is an empty palace a bad sign?
faq.a: No. A palace with no major star is traditionally read by borrowing from the opposite palace. It describes the chart's layout and doesn't mean something is missing from that part of life.

faq.q: What if I choose "Prefer not to say" for gender?
faq.a: Decade Periods need a direction, so the chart uses the male rule and the report notes this.

more.label: Finding your way around the twelve palaces

iching.name: I Ching
iching.background: The I Ching, or Book of Changes, is one of the oldest Chinese classics. Its 64 hexagrams, each built from six lines, describe situations and how they change.
iching.tagline: Cast a hexagram for a question on your mind, using Plum Blossom numerology or the classic three-coin Six Lines method, and read it in plain language.
iching.prepare: No birth details needed. Choose a question category; writing the question out is optional (up to 120 characters).

seo.title: I Ching Reading: Plum Blossom and Six Lines Casting
seo.description: Cast by time, numbers, a random draw or three coins. See your primary hexagram, moving lines and plain-language notes, with visible evidence, for cultural study and self-reflection.

tells.title: The situation you're in
tells.body: Your primary hexagram describes the shape of the matter, with the classical judgment and a plain-language explanation.

tells.title: Where things are moving
tells.body: Moving lines and the resulting hexagram show what is shifting and what it becomes. Plum Blossom also gives a nuclear hexagram for the process along the way.

tells.title: Trigram and line relationships
tells.body: Plum Blossom compares the self and event trigrams. Six Lines adds the full line table: stems and branches, Six Relations, Six Spirits, self and response lines, and a key line chosen for your question.

tells.title: Practical next steps
tells.body: Based on your category, you get a few small actions to try and can decide which ones fit.

method.title: Cast the hexagram
method.body: Plum Blossom can use the current time, two or three numbers, or a random draw. Six Lines tosses three coins six times, from the bottom line up. Time-based casts use your local clock, without true solar time.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: The hexagrams, moving lines and trigram or line relationships all come from fixed rules, and map to structured notes on all 64 hexagrams.

method.title: Read the source text
method.body: Classical judgments and line texts can be expanded in your report, and interpretive chapters end with evidence tags naming the casting method and relationships used.

sample.caption: A made-up Plum Blossom number cast (category: decision)

notes.text: You can improve an outcome by caring for the vessel that makes useful transformation possible.
You can make practical use of support that fits your present capacity.
notes.basis: Event trigram Xun (Wood) feeds self trigram Li (Fire)

faq.q: What's the difference between Plum Blossom and Six Lines?
faq.a: Plum Blossom derives the trigrams and moving line from numbers or time and focuses on how the two trigrams relate. Six Lines builds the hexagram coin toss by coin toss and adds a detailed table for each line.

faq.q: Do I have to write down a question?
faq.a: No, but you do need to pick a category, which selects the notes you see. A specific question makes the reading more useful.

faq.q: What does the score in the report mean?
faq.a: It's a comparison within the rule set that summarizes the reading's overall tilt. It isn't a probability of anything happening.

faq.q: Can I cast again on the same question?
faq.a: Yes, though a different hexagram doesn't mean the first one was wrong. It usually helps to sit with one reading and ask again when circumstances change.

faq.q: Where do the interpretations come from?
faq.a: The judgments and line texts come from the classical I Ching. The plain-language notes are written for our knowledge base, and the report shows the source text alongside them.

more.label: Reading a hexagram from trigrams to lines

qimen.name: Qi Men Dun Jia
qimen.background: Qi Men Dun Jia is a classical Chinese method that maps a moment in time onto a nine-palace grid of Gates, Stars and Deities, traditionally used for thinking through decisions, direction and timing.
qimen.tagline: Lay out the nine palaces for a chosen moment and read how its Gates, Stars, Deities and stems frame your situation, directions and timing.
qimen.prepare: No birth details needed. Choose a question category. The chart uses the current time by default, or any moment and time zone you set.

seo.title: Qi Men Dun Jia Chart: Hour-Based Nine Palaces
seo.description: Generate an hour-based rotating Qi Men chart and explore key indicators, configurations, direction and timing. Rule-based, with visible evidence, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: The shape of the situation
tells.body: Yin or Yang arrangement, the Chief Star and Chief Gate give the overall structure of the moment you chose.

tells.title: Where your key indicators fall
tells.body: Your question category selects the indicators, for example the Open Gate for career or the Life Gate for money, then reads the palace each one falls in.

tells.title: Patterns and constraints
tells.body: The engine flags traditional configurations as well as void, gate-pressure, tomb and punishment markers, so supportive conditions and constraints stay separate.

tells.title: Directions and timing
tells.body: You get the directions and hours that meet the chart's rules, as options to compare with your real plans, not instructions to follow.

method.title: Set the chart from the moment
method.body: We use the hour-based rotating plate with the splitting-and-supplementing method, lodging the center palace with Kun 2. Exact solar-term times set the arrangement and number, then the plates, Gates and Deities are laid out.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: Indicator states, configurations and directions come from fixed rules and map to a structured knowledge base. The same moment and category always give the same chart.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags, and the Technical view includes the full nine-palace table and how the chart was derived.

sample.caption: Chart summary from a made-up moment (category: career)

notes.text: You can test a small next step using the support already visible.
notes.basis: Open Gate palace has a supportive gate and star

notes.text: You can put a northern option on a practical shortlist.
notes.basis: North palace meets the rule with no void or restricting markers

faq.q: Do I need my birth details?
faq.a: No. This is the hour-based form of Qi Men, set from the moment you choose. You only need a question category.

faq.q: Which method does the site use?
faq.a: Hour-based, rotating plate, splitting-and-supplementing method, center palace lodged with Kun 2. It's the only arrangement available at the moment, and the settings are shown in the report's Technical view.

faq.q: Can I change the time of the chart?
faq.a: Yes. The form defaults to now, and you can set any moment and time zone. Web readings use clock time without a true solar time correction.

faq.q: Does a "favorable direction" mean I have to go that way?
faq.a: No. Directions are options selected by the chart's rules. Compare them with your real plans and decide for yourself.

faq.q: Should I use it for big decisions?
faq.a: We wouldn't rely on it alone. The report is meant for cultural study and self-reflection and does not replace medical, legal or financial advice.

more.label: The nine-palace map in Qi Men

tarot.name: Tarot
tarot.background: Tarot is a European card tradition that became a tool for reflection. We use the Rider–Waite–Smith deck of 1909, with Pamela Colman Smith's original artwork.
tarot.tagline: Use the images and symbols of the 78-card deck to look at a question from a different angle.
tarot.prepare: No birth details needed. Choose a spread and a question category; writing the question out is optional (up to 120 characters).

seo.title: Tarot Readings: 78 Cards and Eight Spreads
seo.description: Choose a spread, draw your cards and see what each means in its position, with card interactions and suggestions. Rule-based, using the Rider–Waite–Smith deck, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: Different sides of a question
tells.body: Each position in a spread takes one angle, which helps break a vague worry into parts.

tells.title: What each card means here
tells.body: A card's meaning combines its position, its orientation and your question category, so the same card can read differently from one spread to the next.

tells.title: How the cards relate
tells.body: Major Arcana share, elements, court cards and repeated numbers are counted, and certain card pairings are picked out.

tells.title: Directions to consider
tells.body: The reading ends with small steps to try. The choice always stays with you.

method.title: Choose a spread and draw
method.body: There are eight spreads, from One Card to the Celtic Cross and Year Ahead. The deck has 22 Major and 56 Minor Arcana, and you can choose whether to allow reversed cards.

method.title: Read from a card knowledge base
method.body: Upright and reversed meanings come from a structured knowledge base and combine with position and category. Counting and pairing rules are fixed too.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags for the spread, positions and counts, and every card has a full entry in the Learn section.

notes.text: The King of Cups, with its keywords wisdom, diplomacy, restraint and composure, appears in the Past position as background already in place.
notes.basis: Position: Past; King of Cups, upright

notes.text: You can let feeling become a clear conversation.
notes.basis: Dominant element in this draw: Water

faq.q: Do I need birth details for tarot?
faq.a: No. Tarot doesn't use birth information. Pick a spread and begin.

faq.q: Is a reversed card a bad sign?
faq.a: No. A reversal usually points to a theme turned inward, delayed or overextended; it's another way to read the card. You can also switch off reversals before you start.

faq.q: Do the cards I pick affect the result?
faq.a: Yes. The cards you select feed into the draw, so a given set of picks can be reproduced. You can also let the site draw for you.

faq.q: Can I keep drawing on the same question?
faq.a: You can, but repeated draws tend to add doubt rather than clarity. It usually helps to think through one reading and ask again when something changes.

faq.q: Which deck is this?
faq.a: The 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith deck, with Pamela Colman Smith's original images and Golden Dawn correspondences.

more.label: Learning the 78-card deck through its images

astrology.name: Western Astrology
astrology.background: Natal astrology maps the sky at the moment of your birth onto the tropical zodiac, reading the planets by sign, house and the angles between them.
astrology.tagline: Your birth chart uses planets, signs, houses and aspects to describe recurring themes in personality and relationships.
astrology.prepare: Your birth date, time and place. Without a time you can still generate a chart, but it won't include a rising sign or houses.

seo.title: Western Astrology Birth Chart: Planets, Houses and Aspects
seo.description: Generate a tropical birth chart with Placidus houses by default. Explore Sun, Moon and Ascendant, the twelve houses and aspects, with visible evidence, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: Sun, Moon and Ascendant
tells.body: Three common entry points: core motivation, emotional needs, and how you tend to walk into a new situation.

tells.title: Planets by sign and house
tells.body: Mercury through Pluto, plus the North Node, Chiron and Lilith, by sign and house, each tied to areas like thinking, relating and acting.

tells.title: Aspects and chart patterns
tells.body: The angles between planets, and shapes such as Grand Trines, T-squares and stelliums, show how different needs work together.

tells.title: Life areas and current sky
tells.body: Twelve houses map areas of life, and a current-sky section lists the main planetary transits to your chart for near-term reflection.

method.title: Calculate the sky
method.body: Planetary positions come from the open-source astronomy-engine ephemeris and fall into the tropical zodiac. The Ascendant and houses depend on your birth time and place; Placidus is the default house system.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: Aspects use fixed orbs and chart shapes are detected by rule, then mapped to a structured knowledge base. If Placidus can't be used at very high latitudes, the chart falls back to Whole Sign and says so.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags for the planets, signs and aspects used, so you can check them against the wheel.

sample.caption: Summary of a chart from a made-up birth moment

notes.text: You may enter an unfamiliar setting by making expression personal, while your approach can change as trust develops.
You can use the Grand Trine as a prompt for coordinating needs, without treating it as a ranking or a forecast.
notes.basis: Grand Trine detected in this chart

faq.q: What if I don't know my birth time?
faq.a: You can still get a chart. We calculate for local noon, so planets by sign are still broadly usable, but the Ascendant, Midheaven and houses are left out, and the Moon's position can be off.

faq.q: Which house system do you use?
faq.a: Placidus by default; Whole Sign and Equal are available under advanced options. Placidus doesn't work at very high latitudes, so those charts automatically switch to Whole Sign and are labeled.

faq.q: Why do you need my birthplace?
faq.a: Your Ascendant and houses depend on latitude, longitude and time zone. The closer your birthplace is, the more reliable the houses are.

faq.q: How is it different from Vedic astrology?
faq.a: Western astrology uses the tropical zodiac; Vedic astrology uses the sidereal zodiac (we use the Lahiri ayanamsa). The same planet often lands in the previous sign, and each tradition reads the chart differently.

faq.q: Can a birth chart tell me what will happen?
faq.a: No. It describes symbolic tendencies for cultural study and self-reflection, and makes no claims about specific events. It doesn't replace professional advice.

more.label: Reading the Sun, Moon and rising sign together

vedic.name: Vedic Astrology
vedic.background: Vedic astrology, or Jyotish, is the Indian tradition of astrology. It uses the sidereal zodiac and gives the Moon's position a central role.
vedic.tagline: Your chart is built on the sidereal zodiac, with the Moon's Nakshatra and Vimshottari Dasha periods at the center of the reading.
vedic.prepare: Your birth date, time and place. Without a time you can still generate a chart, but it won't include the Lagna or houses.

seo.title: Vedic Astrology Chart: Nakshatra, Dasha and Navamsa
seo.description: Generate a sidereal Lahiri chart with Rashi and Navamsa. Explore your Moon Nakshatra, Yogas and Vimshottari Dasha periods, with visible evidence, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: Moon Nakshatra
tells.body: Which of the 27 Nakshatras and which Pada your Moon occupies, the main lens for emotional patterns in this tradition.

tells.title: Lagna and the nine grahas
tells.body: Your Lagna and the placements of the Sun, Moon, five planets, Rahu and Ketu, with dignity, retrograde and combustion states.

tells.title: Yogas
tells.body: Twelve traditional combinations, including Gajakesari and Raja Yoga (some in simplified form), are checked and explained when found.

tells.title: Dasha timeline
tells.body: A timeline of Vimshottari Mahadasha and Antardasha periods shows where you are now.

method.title: Convert to the sidereal zodiac
method.body: Planetary longitudes have the Lahiri ayanamsa subtracted. Houses use the Whole Sign system with the Lagna's sign as the first house, and the report includes both the Rashi (D1) and Navamsa (D9) charts.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: Nakshatra and Pada come from the Moon's degree, Dashas start from the Moon's Nakshatra lord, and dignities and Yogas follow fixed rules before mapping to a structured knowledge base.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags for the Nakshatras, grahas and Yogas used. The chart can be drawn in South or North Indian style.

sample.caption: Summary of a chart from a made-up birth moment

notes.text: You may read nuances and check them.
You can make support deliberately accessible.
notes.basis: Kemadruma: none of the five classical planets beside the Moon or in its kendras

faq.q: Why is my sign different from Western astrology?
faq.a: Vedic astrology uses the sidereal zodiac, which sits a little over twenty degrees behind the tropical zodiac most Western charts use, so many planets land in the previous sign. Each result holds within its own rules.

faq.q: Which ayanamsa and house system do you use?
faq.a: The Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa with Whole Sign houses. These are fixed at the moment and noted in the report.

faq.q: What if I don't know my birth time?
faq.a: You can still get a chart based on local noon, which gives usable Nakshatra and Dasha information but no Lagna or houses. If the Moon changed Nakshatra that day, the result may differ, and the report says so.

faq.q: What is a Mahadasha?
faq.a: Vimshottari is a 120-year cycle ruled in turn by nine planets. It starts from your Moon's Nakshatra lord, with the part of that period already elapsed at birth subtracted.

faq.q: Do I have to follow the chants or routines mentioned?
faq.a: No. These are presented as cultural background only, with no promise of any effect, and don't replace professional advice.

numerology.name: Numerology
numerology.background: Numerology treats numbers as a symbolic language. We use the Pythagorean method, which turns your birthday and the letters of your name into a handful of numbers.
numerology.tagline: Your birthday and English name become a few simple numbers you can use to reflect on habits, motivation and the rhythm of a year.
numerology.prepare: Just your Gregorian birth date. An English name is optional. No time, place or gender needed.

seo.title: Numerology Calculator: Life Path and Personal Year
seo.description: Enter your birthday and an optional English name to see your Life Path, Birthday and name numbers plus your Personal Year cycle. Every step is visible, for cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: Life Path and Birthday numbers
tells.body: All the digits of your birth date are added together and reduced to a Life Path number; the Birthday number uses only the day of the month. Master numbers 11, 22 and 33 are kept.

tells.title: Name numbers
tells.body: Your English name gives an Expression number, a Soul number from the vowels, and a Personality number from the consonants.

tells.title: Personal Year, Month and Day
tells.body: Your current Personal Year, Month and Day, with the next nine years listed, serve as prompts for planning and review.

tells.title: Birthday grid and number pairs
tells.body: A grid counts how often 1 through 9 appear in your birthday, and pairing your core numbers gives a compatibility note. An empty cell isn't a flaw.

method.title: Reduce with a fixed method
method.body: All the birth date digits are added in one pass rather than by parts, stopping at 11, 22 or 33 and otherwise reducing to 1–9. Letters use the Pythagorean table, with Y treated as a consonant.

method.title: Match fixed rules to a knowledge base
method.body: Each number and pairing maps to entries in a structured knowledge base. The same birthday and name always give the same result.

method.title: Check the math yourself
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags, and because the rules are simple, you can work the numbers out by hand.

sample.caption: Summary from a made-up birthday and name

notes.text: Life path 1 offers a lens for observing recurring ways of acting.
notes.basis: Birth date digits total 28, reducing to 1

notes.text: Your personal year adds the digits of your birth month and day to the digits of the target year, then reduces to a number from one to nine.

faq.q: Do I need a birth time?
faq.a: No. Numerology only uses the year, month and day. If a saved profile uses a lunar date, it's converted to the Gregorian calendar first.

faq.q: Can I use a Chinese name?
faq.a: Not directly. Name numbers only support English letters and we don't convert Chinese automatically. You can enter an English name or pinyin, or leave it blank.

faq.q: What are master numbers?
faq.a: 11, 22 and 33 are kept rather than reduced further. Personal Year, Month and Day cycles don't use master numbers, so they always run from 1 to 9.

faq.q: When does a Personal Year start?
faq.a: We switch on January 1 each year rather than on your birthday. It's a common convention, and the report explains it.

faq.q: Does this say who I am?
faq.a: It offers one lens, not a psychological measure. The results are meant for cultural study and self-reflection, and your own experience counts for more than any number.

synastry.name: Synastry
synastry.background: Synastry compares two birth charts. Besides Western cross-chart aspects, we also include Chinese comparisons and the Indian Ashtakoot score.
synastry.tagline: Put two charts side by side using BaZi, Zi Wei Dou Shu, Western astrology and Vedic Ashtakoot, to open up a conversation about your differences.
synastry.prepare: Birth dates and times for both people. Signed in, you can pick two saved profiles; otherwise you can enter both on the spot.

seo.title: Synastry: Compare BaZi, Zi Wei, Astrology and Ashtakoot
seo.description: Compare two people through BaZi, Zi Wei Dou Shu, Western cross-chart aspects and the Vedic Ashtakoot score, from communication and love to conflict. For cultural study and reflection.

tells.title: How you communicate and relate
tells.body: Chapters on communication, love, values and money, and conflict patterns gather what the two charts share and where they differ.

tells.title: BaZi and Zi Wei comparisons
tells.body: Day stem and branch relationships, zodiac relations, element differences and each person's Ten Gods for the other, plus Life and Spouse Palace stars in Zi Wei.

tells.title: Cross-chart aspects and overlays
tells.body: Major aspects between the two charts, and which house of one person's chart each of the other's planets falls into.

tells.title: Vedic Ashtakoot score
tells.body: The traditional 36-point score, broken down across eight categories. It's a way to organize a conversation, not a verdict on a relationship.

method.title: Build two charts
method.body: We reuse our BaZi, Zi Wei, Western and Vedic engines to chart each person's birth details separately, with no extra inference.

method.title: Compare by rule, match to a knowledge base
method.body: Relationships, aspects and overlays use fixed rules. Ashtakoot uses the North Indian base table and leaves out disputed cancellation rules. Results map to a structured knowledge base.

method.title: See the evidence for each chapter
method.body: Interpretive chapters end with evidence tags, and the synastry charts show the eight scores and cross-chart aspects.

notes.text: Bhakoot has a full score. This traditional table component has a maximum of 7 points; view it with the other seven without making claims about personal worth, health or relationship outcomes.
Try to repeat the other person's view before making your own request during a small discussion.

faq.q: Does a high score mean we're a good match?
faq.a: No. Ashtakoot is a traditional comparison table meant to help you talk about differences. It doesn't decide a relationship or say anything about either person's worth or health.

faq.q: What is the element difference number?
faq.a: It measures how much your Five Elements distributions differ, from 0 to 100. A higher number means the two are more different; it doesn't mean the relationship is better or worse.

faq.q: Do we both need to know our birth times?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Without a time, BaZi has no hour pillar, the Zi Wei comparison is left out, astrological house overlays are empty, and Ashtakoot uses a provisional noon Moon with a note.

faq.q: Do I need an account?
faq.a: No. You can enter both birth records directly, and they stay in encrypted storage on your device. Signed in, you can choose from saved profiles.

faq.q: Does swapping the two people change the result?
faq.a: It can. The Ashtakoot table is directional: A is scored on the traditional male column and B on the female row, regardless of the genders on your profiles.

faq.q: Should I use this to decide whether to be with someone?
faq.a: We wouldn't. The report is for cultural study and self-reflection. Important decisions belong to your real experience together and, when needed, to professional support.
